adaptationExample.rule: Section 5: the deficit is contextual and applies only to the stated unfamiliar application, never to the underlying skill or acquired competency levels. adaptationExample.scenario: A regional settlement network runs fixed schedules, local codewords and relay etiquette quite unlike the improvised crisis nets the technician knows.
adaptationExample.deficitBasis: SL-trained with documented SL methods: max(0, DZ 20 - SL 15) for Communications (Section 5.3)
adaptationExample.feasibility: If no settlement will give the technician a station slot or equipment, operating on the network is unavailable; exclusion is narrative, not a modifier.
adaptationExample.milestone: Pass traffic correctly on the regional net under its controller's supervision, then independently relay a priority message during a scheduled session.
adaptationExample.rule: Section 5: the deficit is contextual and applies only to the stated unfamiliar application, never to the underlying skill or acquired competency levels. Each distinct GM-approved milestone (normally at least eight active hours plus a documented demonstration) removes five points, capped at the outstanding deficit; elapsed time alone earns nothing. Missing prerequisites, equipment or authority make the affected task unavailable rather than adding a second penalty, and only the largest relevant deficit applies to a single check.

adaptationExample.scenario: A restored clinic acquires pre-collapse digital diagnostic instruments whose calibration procedures assume factory software and standards the technician has never seen.
adaptationExample.deficitBasis: GM-assessed moderate contextual deficit: native calibration practice covers analogue and mechanical devices, not digital instruments with embedded software
adaptationExample.feasibility: Instruments needing proprietary software or standards nobody has cannot be calibrated; they are unavailable, not penalized.
adaptationExample.milestone: Calibrate one digital instrument against a reference with documented error under supervision, then calibrate a second independently.
adaptationExample.rule: Section 5: the deficit is contextual and applies only to the stated unfamiliar application, never to the underlying skill or acquired competency levels. Each distinct GM-approved milestone (normally at least eight active hours plus a documented demonstration) removes five points, capped at the outstanding deficit; elapsed time alone earns nothing. Missing prerequisites, equipment or authority make the affected task unavailable rather than adding a second penalty, and only the largest relevant deficit applies to a single check.

advantage.description: Recognizing workable clay beds, temper materials and kiln fuel in the landscape by look, feel and plasticity.

sourcebook.resourceRule: Catalogue requirements, prerequisite levels, CCDD-19 CDR thresholds, hours and assessment remain mandatory. adaptationExample.scenario: A trader asks for glazed food storage jars, requiring glazes the potter has never made safely.
adaptationExample.deficitBasis: GM-assessed moderate contextual deficit: native pottery is unglazed or ash-glazed, and safe glaze chemistry is unfamiliar
adaptationExample.feasibility: Without safe glaze materials, glazed food wares are unavailable rather than penalized.
adaptationExample.milestone: Develop a glaze from tested local materials and fire jars that pass a leach and soak test, reviewed by an experienced potter.
adaptationExample.rule: Section 5: the deficit is contextual and applies only to the stated unfamiliar application, never to the underlying skill or acquired competency levels. Each distinct GM-approved milestone (normally at least eight active hours plus a documented demonstration) removes five points, capped at the outstanding deficit; elapsed time alone earns nothing. Missing prerequisites, equipment or authority make the affected task unavailable rather than adding a second penalty, and only the largest relevant deficit applies to a single check.

advantage.verification: Once per in-world day, halve routine setup time for the stated familiar task only; never applies to training, assessment or hazardous procedures, and grants no success, reroll or bonus.

sourcebook.resourceRule: Catalogue requirements, prerequisite levels, CCDD-19 CDR thresholds, hours and assessment remain mandatory. adaptationExample.scenario: The specialist joins a coastal settlement where rescues mean tidal cliffs and small boats, after training among inland ruins and forests.
adaptationExample.deficitBasis: The GM judges search method transfers, but tides, cliff hazards and boat searching are unfamiliar and must be learned with local crews.
adaptationExample.feasibility: Without a boat or a crew willing to take the specialist out, sea searches are not possible; that is feasibility, not deficit.
adaptationExample.milestone: Take part in a supervised tidal-cliff search exercise with the local crew and a written debrief, reviewed by an experienced boat captain.
adaptationExample.rule: Section 5: the deficit is contextual and applies only to the stated unfamiliar application, never to the underlying skill or acquired competency levels. Each distinct GM-approved milestone (normally at least eight active hours plus a documented demonstration) removes five points, capped at the outstanding deficit; elapsed time alone earns nothing. Missing prerequisites, equipment or authority make the affected task unavailable rather than adding a second penalty, and only the largest relevant deficit applies to a single check.

adaptationExample.scenario: Moving into the settlement era, a displaced character whose history records farm work chooses Agriculture and must farm unfamiliar soil.
adaptationExample.deficitBasis: SL-trained with documented SL methods: max(0, DZ 15 - SL 10) for Agriculture (Section 5.3)
adaptationExample.feasibility: Without seed or tools, farming cannot start; supplies limit the work rather than adding to the deficit.
adaptationExample.milestone: Bring a plot to harvest with a written planting record, reviewed by an experienced local farmer.
adaptationExample.rule: Section 5: the deficit is contextual and applies only to the stated unfamiliar application, never to the underlying skill or acquired competency levels. Each distinct GM-approved milestone (normally at least eight active hours plus a documented demonstration) removes five points, capped at the outstanding deficit; elapsed time alone earns nothing. Missing prerequisites, equipment or authority make the affected task unavailable rather than adding a second penalty, and only the largest relevant deficit applies to a single check.
